questions.q: How does this lesson build dim_customers so it keeps real history?
options: On top of a snapshot, using the dbt_valid_from/dbt_valid_to columns the snapshot generates for SCD Type 2
By overwriting the table completely on every run with no history
By hand-writing a MERGE statement inside the model, exactly like the Snowflake capstone
History isn't possible in dbt at all
questions.explain: The snapshot captures row-level history over time and generates dbt_valid_from/dbt_valid_to automatically — the SCD Type 2 mechanism from Chapter 5.

questions.q: Why is fct_orders materialized as incremental in this lesson?
options: So it only processes new/changed rows after the first run instead of a full rebuild every time
Because incremental models cannot be tested
Incremental materialization is required for every dbt model regardless of size
To avoid writing any SQL in the model
questions.explain: Incremental materialization, with a merge strategy and unique_key, avoids reprocessing the entire fact table on every run.

questions.q: What is a singular test, according to this lesson?
options: A one-off SQL query encoding a business rule; the build fails if it returns any rows
A generic test that runs automatically with no SQL needed
A test that can only check for NULL values
A test that runs exactly once and is then deleted
questions.explain: The lesson's example (assert_fct_orders_amount_not_negative.sql) is a singular test: it fails the build if the query returns any rows.

questions.q: What makes the generated dbt Docs site show real information instead of blank tooltips?
options: Writing real descriptions for every mart-layer model and column in schema.yml before running dbt docs generate
Running dbt docs generate alone, with no descriptions written anywhere
Manually editing the generated HTML file after the fact
Documentation cannot be generated for marts-layer models
questions.explain: dbt docs generate pulls directly from the descriptions already written in schema.yml — without them, the docs site has nothing to show.

questions.q: In fct_orders's join to dim_customers, which key does the fact table join on?
options: The dimension's surrogate key (customer_key), filtered to the current row with is_current
The customer's natural/business key directly, with no surrogate key involved
A random row from the dimension with no join condition
There is no join between the fact and dimension tables
questions.explain: The fact table joins on customer_key (the surrogate key) and filters to c.is_current, which is what makes SCD Type 2 history work correctly.
